statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ front-month trades near 29,565.25 (+0.14%) and remains inside the 29,530.50-29,683.50 band, roughly 0.52% wide, that has now contained about sixteen hours of trade with the session high still unretested. Tail holds at 5 because that path is contained and two-way. Stress eases to 55: Brent has cooled to about $97.11 (+0.9%) from a $97.50 six-week high and WTI is near $92.28 at a three-month high, while Friday's 162k August payrolls hold Fed rate-hike odds for next week near 60%. US cash equity, Treasury and Cboe markets are shut for Labor Day and CME equity futures halt at 17:00 UTC.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and Tail remains far below the block threshold in every hour of this outlook. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the shortened Labor Day futures halt, and secondarily at the 22:00 UTC restart that opens the Tuesday trade date after five closed hours. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active throughout. This is a descriptive market-regime assessment, not personal financial advice.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold a sixteen-hour band into the Labor Day halt as Brent cools from its six-week high and rate-hike odds stay near 60%
body:
The observed price path remains the strongest evidence this hour and it continues to argue for a low tail value. The band from 29,530.50 to 29,683.50, about 0.52% wide, has now contained roughly sixteen hours of trade. NQ is near 29,565.25, up 0.14% on a 29,535.25 open, and the delayed cross-asset snapshot taken at 13:03 UTC put the contract nearer +0.03%, so the drift within the hour has been marginally lower and still well inside the band. The session high was made early, rejected, and has not been retested. Containment with working retracements is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency that overwhelms a mean-reversion approach, so Tail stays at 5.

Energy remains the loudest cross-asset input and it has cooled slightly further within the hour. Brent is near $97.11, up about 0.9% on the day after printing a six-week high close to $97.50; WTI is near $92.28, up about 0.9% and testing three-month highs. The driver is the US-Iran tanker conflict in and around the Strait of Hormuz: US strikes on three Iranian tankers over the weekend, Iranian ballistic-missile fire toward US warships, and an unresolved Iranian threat of a restricted maritime zone. That is a genuine escalation, but it is a months-old conflict rather than a new discontinuity, and equity futures are still not transmitting it.

The macro backdrop firmed over the weekend and has not changed since. August non-farm payrolls printed 162,000 against a 56,000 consensus with unemployment steady at 4.1%, and futures pricing implies roughly a 60% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike at next week's meeting, up from about 50% before the release. Gold is down about 0.8% near $4,390 on the same repricing. Per the calibration used here, that repricing raises Stress and shapes the event calendar rather than raising path risk on its own; PPI on 10 September and CPI on 11 September are the checkpoints where it would next be tested.

Cross-asset confirmation is deliberately incomplete today. US cash equity, Treasury and Cboe markets are closed for Labor Day, so the last H.15 curve remains 3 September at 4.34% for the two-year, 4.77% for the ten-year and 5.25% for the thirty-year, and VIX last printed near 15.14 at Friday's close. The delayed futures snapshot shows the Nasdaq contract marginally higher against S&P futures near -0.16% and Dow futures near -0.46%, a split that echoes Friday's cash session, where the Nasdaq-100 rose 0.21% while the S&P 500 fell 0.38% and the Dow lost 0.51%. Asian trade was strongly chip-led, with the Nikkei up 2.1%, the Kospi up 4.6%, SK Hynix up 8.1% and Samsung up 5.7%. A regional semiconductor bid that does not lift NQ out of a sixteen-hour band is a divergence, not the aligned amplifier stack that would justify a higher tail value.

The conditional structure of the next hours is driven by venue mechanics rather than by any observed trend. CME equity futures halt at 17:00 UTC and reopen at 22:00 UTC for the Tuesday trade date, so a narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC danger window is flagged for the European cash close into that halt, and the restart hour carries a small lift for reopen-gap risk. Confidence is 85: the price path, oil, the payrolls outcome, rate-hike pricing and the calendar are all current and verified, while the holiday closure of yield and volatility venues is a known market condition rather than an evidence gap.

lookbackSummary: 23 of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday afternoon and evening, stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart to carry reopen-gap risk, eased to 6 and then 5 once that restart proved orderly, lifted to 7 as the overnight high extended, and settled back to 6 and then a flat 5 across the last six hours as that high was retraced and left unretested. Every available hour mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress ranged from 54 to 60, peaking at the 20:00 UTC hour before the reopen and easing through the Asian session as the oil bid held without transmitting into index futures. Confidence sat between 84 and 86 throughout, reflecting a continuously available futures price path against holiday-closed yield and volatility venues.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the remainder of a holiday afternoon traded against closed US cash equity, Treasury and Cboe markets, a shortened futures session that halts at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, and the Tuesday Asian session into the European cash open and the hour before the US cash reopen. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band in every hour: 5 for the current hour, 6 across the holiday afternoon where thinned depth meets no US cash backstop, 6 to 8 in the flagged 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European close into the halt, 5 through the halted hours where no tradable path exists, 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart for reopen-gap risk, and 6 to 7 across the Asian session into Tuesday's European morning. Every hour therefore maps to EA_ON and green. Stress runs from 50 during the closure to 58 in the pre-halt window and back to 57 by the end of the horizon, and confidence decays from 85 to 67 as the assessment moves further from currently observed evidence. The escalation conditions that would change this picture are explicit: a sustained loss of 29,530.50 with no working retracement, repeated extension after failed pullbacks at the restart or the European open, or an oil extension that finally transmits into index futures instead of diverging from them.
